page_title: Web application from scratch, Part I

summary.title: Web application from scratch, Part I
summary.one_liner: You learn how HTTP requests and responses are structured on the wire and how to build a basic Python socket web server that parses requests and serves files from disk using only the standard library.
takeaways: HTTP requests are CRLF-separated lines: a request line (method, path, version), headers, a blank line, then an optional body; responses mirror this with a status line.
A minimal server can be built with socket.socket, bind, listen, and accept, then sendall a fixed response.
Parsing requests can be done with a generator that reads from the socket and yields lines, wrapped in a Request class with from_socket.
Malformed requests should get a 400 response rather than crashing the server; unsupported methods get 405 and missing files get 404.
serve_file maps URL paths to files under a root directory, checks the resolved path stays inside it, and uses sendfile to stream the file.
summary.summary: This is Part I of a series that builds a Python web application and its HTTP server using only the standard library, deliberately ignoring WSGI. It first explains the HTTP request and response wire format, then incrementally builds a server: a socket that returns a fixed response, a looping accept, a line-reading generator, and a Request class. It adds 400, 404 and 405 error responses and finishes with a serve_file function that serves files from a www directory. Part II is said to cover Server and Response abstractions and concurrency.
